paragraphs: International Business Machines Corporation (IBM or the company) was incorporated in the State of New York on June 16, 1911, as the Computing-Tabulating-Recording Co. (C-T-R), a consolidation of the Computing Scale Co. of America, the Tabulating Machine Co. and The International Time Recording Co. of New York. Since that time, IBM has focused on the intersection of business insight and technological innovation, and its operations and aims have been international in nature. This was signaled over 100 years ago, in 1924, when C-T-R changed its name to International Business Machines Corporation. And it continues today—we create sustained value for clients by helping them leverage the power of hybrid cloud and artificial intelligence (AI). Our hybrid cloud platform and AI technology support clients' digital transformations and helps them reimagine critical workflows, at scale, and modernize applications to increase agility, drive innovation and create operational efficiencies. Our offerings draw from leading IBM capabilities in software, consulting services capability to deliver business outcomes, and deep incumbency in mission-critical infrastructure, all bolstered by one of the world's leading research organizations.
The following information is included in IBM's 2025 Annual Report to Stockholders and is incorporated by reference:
Business Segments and Capabilities—pages 12 to 14.

We proactively partner with a broad variety of companies including hyperscalers, service providers, global system integrators, and software and hardware vendors. We work alongside our partners to deliver end-to-end solutions that address our clients' complex business challenges while accelerating growth. Our strategic partners include: Adobe, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft, Oracle, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce, Samsung Electronics and SAP, among others.
Companies with which we have strategic partnerships in some areas may be competitors in other areas.

IBM is a globally integrated enterprise that participates in a highly competitive environment. Our competitors vary by industry segment, and range from large multinational enterprises to smaller, more narrowly focused entities. Across our business segments, we recognize hundreds of competitors worldwide and as we execute our hybrid cloud and AI strategy, we are regularly exposed to new competitors.

Our principal methods of competition are: technology innovation; performance; price; quality; brand; our breadth of capabilities, products and services; talent; client relationships and trust; the ability to deliver business value to clients; and service and support. In order to maintain leadership, we optimize our portfolio with organic and inorganic innovations and effective resource allocation. These investments not only drive current performance but will extend our innovation leadership into the future.

Our breadth and depth of expertise enables us to take different technologies and bring them together to solve the most pressing business issues of our clients. We differentiate from other providers by bringing together incumbency with enterprises, deep expertise in technology, industries and business processes, a broad go-to-market reach including an ecosystem of partners and alliances, and a strong focus on innovation. All of these attributes position IBM for accelerated growth now and prepare us for the next set of business opportunities, such as quantum computing.
Overall, the company is the leader or among the leaders in each of our business segments. A summary of the competitive environment for each business segment is included below:

The depth, breadth, and innovation of our software offerings, coupled with our global reach, deep industry expertise and research capabilities help differentiate our offerings from our competitors. Our hybrid cloud and AI platforms allow clients to realize their digital and AI transformations across the applications, data, and environments in which they operate. The principal competitors in this segment include: Alphabet (Google), Amazon, BMC, Broadcom, Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP and Splunk, a CISCO Company. We also compete with smaller, niche competitors in specific geographic regions or product segments.

Consulting integrates strategy, experience design, technology and operations expertise by domain across industries to deliver transformation for clients. Consulting operates in a highly competitive, dynamic market that spans business consulting, systems integration, application development and management, and business process outsourcing services. Our competitors include global firms such as Accenture, Capgemini, India-based service providers, management consulting firms, the consulting practices of public accounting firms, engineering service providers, and niche specialists. Our competitive position is supported by industry expertise; hybrid cloud, data, and AI capabilities; and the use of IBM technology and ecosystem partners to deliver solutions aligned to clients' strategic priorities.

IBM is well positioned in the growing hybrid cloud infrastructure market, providing on-premises and cloud-based server and storage solutions. We gain advantage and differentiation through investments in higher-value capabilities, including security, scalability, and reliability, designed especially for mission-critical and AI workloads. In addition, we offer a portfolio of life-cycle services for hybrid cloud infrastructure deployment. Our principal competitors include: Dell Technologies, Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Intel, NetApp and Pure Storage as well as original device manufacturers (ODMs) who provide systems that are re-branded. Further, cloud service providers are leveraging innovation in technology and service delivery to compete with traditional providers and to offer additional routes to market for server and storage systems.

Financing provides client and commercial financing, facilitating IBM clients' acquisition of hardware, software and services. Financing's ability to manage credit and residual value risk generates a competitive advantage for the company. The key competitive factors include: interest rates charged, IT product experience, client service, contract flexibility, ease of doing business, global capabilities and residual values. In client and commercial financing, Financing primarily competes with non-captive financing entities and financial institutions.

paragraphs: Downturn in Economic Environment and Client Spending Budgets Could Impact the Company's Business: If overall demand for IBM's products and solutions decreases, whether due to general economic conditions, or a shift in client buying patterns, the company's revenue and profit could be impacted.

Failure of Innovation Initiatives Could Impact the Long-Term Success of the Company: IBM has moved into areas, including those that incorporate or utilize hybrid cloud, AI, quantum and other disruptive technologies, in which it can differentiate itself through responsible innovation, by leveraging its investments in R&D and attracting a successful developer ecosystem. If IBM is unable to continue its cutting-edge innovation in a highly competitive and rapidly evolving environment or is unable to commercialize such innovations, expand and scale them with sufficient speed and versatility or is unable to attract a successful developer ecosystem, the company could fail in its ongoing efforts to maintain and increase its market share and its profit margins.

Damage to IBM's Reputation Could Impact the Company's Business: IBM has one of the strongest brand names in the world, and its brand and overall reputation could be negatively impacted by many factors, including if the company does not continue to be recognized for its industry leading technology and solutions and as a hybrid cloud and AI leader. IBM's reputation is potentially susceptible to damage by events such as significant disputes with clients, product defects, internal control deficiencies, delivery failures, cybersecurity incidents, government investigations or legal proceedings or actions of current or former clients, directors, employees, competitors, vendors, alliance partners or joint venture partners. If the
company's brand image is tarnished by negative perceptions, its ability to attract and retain customers, talent and ecosystem partners could be impacted.

Risks from Investing in Growth Opportunities Could Impact the Company's Business: The company continues to invest significantly in key strategic areas, including AI, to drive revenue growth and market share gains. Client adoption rates and viable economic models are less certain in the high-value, highly competitive, and rapidly-growing segments. Additionally, emerging business and delivery models may unfavorably impact demand and profitability for our other products or services. If the company does not adequately and timely anticipate and respond to changes in customer and market preferences, competitive actions, disruptive technologies, emerging business models and ecosystems, the client demand for our products or services may decline or IBM's costs may increase.

IBM's Intellectual Property Portfolio May Not Prevent Competitive Offerings, and IBM May Not Be Able to Obtain Necessary Licenses: The company's patents and other intellectual property may not prevent competitors from independently developing products and services similar to or duplicative to the company's, nor can there be any assurance that the resources invested by the company to protect its intellectual property will be sufficient or that the company's intellectual property portfolio will adequately deter misappropriation or improper use of the company's technology. In addition, the company may be the target of aggressive and opportunistic enforcement of patents by third parties, including non-practicing entities. Also, there can be no assurances that IBM will be able to obtain from third parties the licenses it needs in the future. The company's ability to protect its intellectual property could also be impacted by a lack of effective legal protections as well as changes to existing laws, legal principles and regulations governing intellectual property, including the ownership and protection of patents.

paragraphs: International Business Machines Corporation (IBM 或本公司) 於 1911 年 6 月 16 日在紐約州註冊成立，原名為 Computing-Tabulating-Recording Co. (C-T-R)，為 Computing Scale Co. of America、Tabulating Machine Co. 及 The International Time Recording Co. of New York 的合併企業。自那時起，IBM 便專注於商業洞察與科技創新交會之處，其營運與目標皆具國際性。這一點在 100 多年前的 1924 年已明顯體現，當時 C-T-R 更名為 International Business Machines Corporation。而今日我們持續如此—透過協助客戶善用混合雲端與人工智慧 (AI) 的力量，創造可持續的價值。我們的混合雲端平台與 AI 技術支援客戶的數位轉型，協助他們在規模上重新設計關鍵作業流程，並現代化應用程式以提高靈活性、推動創新並創造運營效率。我們的產品與服務結合 IBM 在軟體、諮詢服務方面的專業能力，以及在關鍵基礎設施領域的深厚經驗，並由全球頂尖的研究機構支援。
IBM 2025 年年度股東報告書中包含以下資訊，並作為參考資料引用：
業務分部與能力—第 12 至 14 頁。

我們積極與多種類型的公司合作，包括超大型資料中心運營商、服務供應商、全球系統整合商，以及軟體與硬體供應商。我們與合作夥伴共同提供端到端解決方案，以應對客戶複雜的商業挑戰，同時加速成長。我們的戰略合作夥伴包括：Adobe、Amazon Web Services (AWS)、Microsoft、Oracle、Palo Alto Networks、Salesforce、Samsung Electronics 和 SAP，以及其他公司。
與我們在某些領域有戰略合作關係的公司，可能在其他領域成為競爭對手。
IBM 是一家全球整合企業，參與高度競爭的環境。我們的競爭對手因產業分部而異，範圍從大型跨國企業到較小且專注於特定領域的企業。在各個業務分部中，我們在全球認知到數百家競爭對手，而隨著我們執行混合雲端與 AI 策略，我們經常面對新的競爭對手。
我們的主要競爭方式包括：科技創新；性能；價格；品質；品牌；我們在能力、產品與服務的廣度；人才；客戶關係與信任；為客戶創造商業價值的能力；以及服務與支援。為維持領導地位，我們透過內生與外生創新，以及有效的資源配置，優化產品組合。這些投資不僅推動現有表現，也將我們的創新領導地位延伸至未來。
我們在廣度與深度的專業知識，使我們能將不同科技整合起來，解決客戶最迫切的商業問題。我們透過結合企業經驗、對科技、產業與商業流程的深厚專業知識、廣泛的市場接觸包括合作夥伴與聯盟生態系，以及對創新強烈的關注，與其他供應商區隔。這些特質使 IBM 能夠加速成長，並為未來的商業機會做好準備，例如量子計算。
整體而言，本公司在各個業務分部中均為領導者或其中一員。以下為各業務分部競爭環境的總結：

我們軟體產品的深度、廣度與創新性，加上我們的全球佈局、深厚的產業經驗與研究能力，有助於我們的產品與競爭對手區隔。我們的混合雲與人工智慧平台讓客戶能在其運作的應用程式、資料與環境中實現數位與人工智慧的轉型。此分部的主要競爭對手包括：Alphabet (Google)、Amazon、BMC、Broadcom、Microsoft、Oracle、Salesforce、SAP 以及 Splunk，為 CISCO 公司。我們也與一些較小、專注特定地理區域或產品分部的競爭對手競爭。

顧問服務整合跨產業的策略、經驗設計、科技與運營專業知識，為客戶提供轉型方案。顧問服務運作於高度競爭且動態的市場，涵蓋企業諮詢、系統整合、應用程式開發與管理，以及企業流程外包服務。我們的競爭對手包括 Accenture、Capgemini、印度的服務供應商、管理諮詢公司、會計師事務所的諮詢部門、工程服務供應商以及專門領域的專家。我們的競爭優勢來自產業專業知識、混合雲、資料與人工智慧能力，以及使用 IBM 科技與生態系夥伴來提供符合客戶戰略優先順序的解決方案。

IBM 在成長中的混合雲基礎設施市場中處於優勢地位，提供企業內部與雲端的伺服器與儲存解決方案。我們透過投資高價值能力，包括安全性、可擴展性與可靠性，特別針對關鍵任務與人工智慧工作負載設計，以取得優勢與區隔。此外，我們提供一套混合雲基礎設施部署的全生命週期服務。我們的主要競爭對手包括：Dell Technologies、Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE)、Intel、NetApp 以及 Pure Storage，以及提供系統並重新品牌的原始設備製造商 (ODMs)。此外，雲端服務供應商正透過科技與服務交付的創新，與傳統供應商競爭，並為伺服器與儲存系統提供額外的市場通路。
融資提供客戶與商業融資，協助 IBM 客戶取得硬體、軟體與服務。融資管理信用與殘值風險的能力，為本公司帶來競爭優勢。關鍵競爭因素包括：所收取的利率、IT 產品經驗、客戶服務、契約靈活性、營運便利性、全球能力與殘值。在客戶與商業融資方面，融資主要與非專屬融資機構與金融機構競爭。

paragraphs: 經濟環境走弱及客戶預算支出減少可能影響本公司的營業：若IBM產品及解決方案的總體需求減少，無論是因總體經濟條件或客戶購買新模式的改變，本公司營業收入及利潤可能受到影響。

創新計畫失敗可能影響本公司長期成功：IBM已進入包括混合雲、人工智慧、量子及其他顛覆性技術等領域，在這些領域中，IBM可透過負責任的創新，利用其在研究與發展上的投資，並吸引成功的開發者生態系統，以區隔自身。若IBM無法在高度競爭且快速變化的環境中持續進行尖端創新，或無法將創新商品化，並以足夠的速度與靈活性擴展與規模化，或無法吸引成功的開發者生態系統，本公司可能在維持及增加市場佔有率及利潤率的持續努力中失敗。
IBM聲譽受損可能影響本公司營業：IBM擁有全球最強的商標之一，其品牌及整體聲譽可能因多種因素而受到負面影響，包括本公司未能持續被認可為產業領先的技術與解決方案提供者，以及混合雲與人工智慧領導者。IBM的聲譽可能因重大與客戶的爭議、產品缺陷、內部控制缺失、交付失敗、網路安全事件、政府調查或法律程序，或現任或前客戶、董事、員工、競爭對手、供應商、合作夥伴或合資企業夥伴的行為而受到損害。若
本公司品牌形象因負面觀感而受損，其吸引並留住客戶、人才及生態系統夥伴的能力可能受到影響。

投資成長機會的風險可能影響本公司的業務：本公司持續在關鍵戰略領域，包括人工智慧（AI），進行大量投資，以推動營業收入成長及市場佔有率提升。在高價值、高度競爭且快速成長的領域中，客戶採用率及可行的經濟模式較難預測。此外，新興的業務與交付模式可能不利於我們其他產品或服務的需求與獲利。若本公司未能充分且及時預見並回應客戶與市場偏好、競爭行動、顛覆性技術、新興業務模式與生態系統的變化，客戶對本公司產品或服務的需求可能下降，或IBM的營運成本可能增加。

IBM的智慧財產權組合可能無法防止競爭產品，且IBM可能無法取得必要的授權：本公司的專利及其他智慧財產權可能無法阻止競爭對手獨立開發與本公司產品或服務相似或重複的產品或服務，亦無法確保本公司投入資源保護智慧財產權足夠，或本公司智慧財產權組合足夠防止誤用或不當使用本公司的技術。此外，本公司可能成為第三方，包括非實體專利持有者，對專利進行積極且機會主義的執行目標。另外，無法確保IBM將來能夠從第三方取得所需的授權。本公司保護智慧財產權的能力也可能受到缺乏有效的法律保護以及現有法律、法律原則與智慧財產權相關法規變動的影響，包括專利的所有權與保護。
